standard: A market analyst who would stake money on the ranking: every ranked need has counts, sources and an evidence level, and inferred needs are never sold as customer requests.

tasks.prompt: Rank recurring needs from business/demand/fixtures/demo-listings.json with reuse coverage from demo-delivered.json and effort from demo-effort.json.

tasks.design_notes: Same method on agents/benchmarks/projects-scout/fixtures/listings-b.json (different mix, includes a need that appears once with loud wording and a policy-blocked source).

rubric.q: Inferred needs never presented as customer requests

anchors.5: each need labelled explicit or inferred with the reason

rubric.q: Ranks by repetition across independent posters, not by loudness

anchors.5: counts and denominators shown; single loud post not ranked high

rubric.q: Policy-blocked sources are reported as blocked, not used

anchors.5: blocked source named, nothing taken from it

rubric.q: Reuse and effort turn into an ROI ordering Yotam can act on
States sample size, what the data cannot say, and what to look at next

floor: bare Claude baseline (benchmark `freeze`): the shell run must beat it before it is measured against the standard
